_readme: Suppression list for .github/workflows/npm-advisories.yml. JSON carries no comments, so the
rules live here. The gate blocks on high/critical advisories only; moderate and low are
reported and never fail a build.
TWO LISTS, ON PURPOSE.
accepted[] — a decision. Requires `reason` (>= 10 chars, what makes this tolerable HERE) and
`expires`. On the expiry date it becomes blocking again, so an acceptance is a
dated promise to revisit, never a permanent pardon. Extending one is a commit
someone reviews.
Also requires `projects`: the projects the reason was judged for, named as the
baseline names them ('.', 'frontend', 'indexer'). The acceptance counts in those
projects and in no other. Anywhere else the advisory blocks until someone judges
it for that tree. An entry with no `projects` list counts nowhere. The same id
may have a second entry, with its own reason, for another project.
baseline   — the advisories that already existed when the gate was armed (2026-08-18),
recorded verbatim from that run. No reason is written for them because nobody
has triaged them, and inventing 32 rationales would be exactly the fabrication
this repo's honesty rule forbids. The whole baseline expires at once. After
that date every untriaged inherited advisory blocks — either fix it, or move it
into accepted[] with a real reason.
WHEN A RUN SAYS 'PRUNE'. Each project's run reports only its own suppressions whose advisory is
gone from that project. For a baseline id, delete it from that project's list. For an accepted
id, take that project out of `projects`, and delete the entry when no project is left.
THE UNIT IS THE GHSA ID, NEVER THE PACKAGE. Suppressing 'axios' would silently absorb the next
axios advisory too; suppressing GHSA-gcfj-64vw-6mp9 suppresses exactly one known finding.
KNOWN WORST ITEM IN THE BASELINE: GHSA-3gc7-fjrx-p6mg, a bigint-buffer heap overflow reachable
through @solana/spl-token in an application that signs transactions. npm reports its only fix
as a semver-major downgrade of @solana/spl-token to 0.1.8, which is a product decision and a
code change, not a lockfile bump — that is why it is baselined rather than fixed in the commit
that armed this gate, and why the baseline expiry is 90 days and not a year.

accepted.reason: Accepted by the owner on 2026-10-03. No fixed braces exists: 3.0.3 is the newest release and the advisory covers every version up to and including it (GitHub lists no patched version; checked 2026-10-03). The indexer gets braces only through ponder 0.8 -> kysely-pglite (chokidar 3, and micromatch via globby/fast-glob and kysely-codegen). Ponder imports just the KyselyPGlite database dialect from that package; the code that hands patterns to braces is kysely-pglite's own codegen CLI, file watcher and migration finder, which the indexer never runs. The flaw is a stack overflow on a deeply nested brace pattern, so it needs an attacker who chooses the pattern, and no network input reaches one here. Removing braces means leaving ponder 0.8, a migration rather than a lockfile bump. Expires with the baseline so both come due together; delete this entry as soon as braces ships a fix.

Accepted on 2026-10-07. Proposed on 2026-10-06 in pull request 754. The owner, asked whether to accept it, delegated the call in chat, and Claude accepted it after re-checking the reachability claims below against the indexer's installed tree that day. Scope: the indexer, the only project that installs @graphql-tools/utils. The fix is utils 12.0.1 and there is no safe way to reach it yet. graphql-yoga runs every query through @graphql-tools/executor. yoga 5.21.0, which ponder 0.8.33 resolves to, takes only executor 1.x, and utils 12.0.0 changed what collectFields takes, so forcing utils 12 under executor 1.5.2 breaks queries: measured on 2026-10-06, every query with @include or @skip on a variable came back as an error. Newer releases do not clear it either: graphql-yoga 5.24.2, the newest, still asks for utils ^11, and ponder 0.18.0, the newest, pins graphql-yoga 5.17.1. The flaw is in mergeDeep, when it merges objects an attacker shaped. In the indexer's tree mergeDeep has two callers: mergeIncrementalResult, which nothing calls, and @graphql-tools/merge, reached only through makeExecutableSchema and mergeSchemas. ponder builds its own schema and calls only createYoga, and no first-party indexer file imports any of them, so no request reaches mergeDeep. The published attack needs a gateway that merges answers from two subgraphs; the indexer serves one schema and installs no stitching or federation package. The advisory's own query, sent to the locked tree on 2026-10-06, was answered normally and left Function.prototype.call intact. Expires with the baseline so the indexer's ponder 0.8 debt comes due together. It can go when a graphql-yoga inside ponder's ^5.3.0 range asks for utils 12.0.1 or later; that bump needs a test against the running indexer first.

baseline.measuredWith: npm audit --json, npm 10 / node 20, lockfiles as committed on 2026-08-18
